label: App shell
purpose: The chrome nearly every product needs — brand, navigation, and a content region — as one responsive frame, so a builder adapts the destinations and content rather than re-deciding the shell.
when_to_use: The top-level frame of an application (a social app, a dashboard product, any multi-destination tool).
when_not_to_use: A single marketing page or a pushed detail screen — use a marketing block or a plain AppBar with a back button instead.
composition: Desktop (md+) — the library Sidebar with the brand Logo in its header and the destinations as its menu, beside a SidebarInset whose header carries the collapse trigger and the current section, then the scrollable content.
Mobile — a branded AppBar (the wordmark's home in product chrome) on top, the scrollable content, and a BottomNavItem row along the bottom.
One responsive component (useIsMobile) switches between the two so the same destinations drive both.
primary_action: None — chrome carries NO primary Button, so the app's own primary action (inside the content) is never shadowed. The active destination is marked by aria-current + weight/background, never colour alone.
responsive: A single breakpoint (useIsMobile): desktop shows the Sidebar + inset; mobile shows the AppBar + bottom nav. Content scrolls within its region; the chrome does not.
accessibility: the selected destination carries aria-current='page' plus a weight/background change, never colour alone
the brand is the Logo COMPONENT (never typeset), sized for chrome (46px), and swaps black/white by theme
the mobile nav is a <nav aria-label='Primary'>; the desktop collapse control is the labelled SidebarTrigger
content: Ships a realistic four-destination social layout (Home / Search / Alerts / Profile) as PLACEHOLDER structure — adapt the destinations and content, keep the frame.
anti_patterns: typesetting the brand as text instead of the Logo component
a filled primary Button in the shell chrome (it competes with the screen's real primary)
marking the active destination by colour alone with no aria-current / weight change
assumptions: Destinations are PLACEHOLDER (Home / Search / Alerts / Profile) — replace with the product's real sections.
The brand is the 2one Logo; swap in your own via the same slot when this is built for another brand.
Navigation is local state here; wire the destinations to your router in a real app.

references.note: shadcn ships a sidebar block but no full app shell with a mobile bottom-nav counterpart (its canonical blocks are dashboard, sidebar, login, signup — https://ui.shadcn.com/blocks). So this pattern composes the shadcn Sidebar PRIMITIVE with the 2one-authored AppBar / BottomNavItem / Logo — every part a real, in-repo component; nothing invented.
